title: Superconducting magnets for high-power plasma thrusters
bottleneck: Advanced plasma thrusters like VASIMR promise variable thrust and high efficiency at power levels where conventional electric propulsion cannot compete — but only with strong, lightweight magnetic nozzles. Superconducting magnets would deliver the field strength without prohibitive power draw, yet space-rated superconductors must survive launch vibration, operate for years, and be cooled in vacuum without heavy cryocoolers. Quench protection — a magnet suddenly going resistive — in an autonomous deep-space engine is unsolved.
why_it_blocks: Without high-field magnets, plasma thrusters stay capped at low power and cannot deliver the fast Mars transits or heavy cargo hauls that justify their development cost.
current_state: VASIMR's VX-200 demonstrated ~200 kW operation with conventional magnets in ground tests; Ad Astra continues development. No superconducting plasma thruster has flown.
